storyboard.claim: The book's advice assumes autonomy and money that many readers do not have.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried professional thinking, the reader who is not the privileged founder.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the critique after the framework was summarised.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the structural blind spot the narrator says the book ignores.

storyboard.claim: The listed advice (hire an admin, 50% to product) is glib for most workers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz points at the viewer with a smirk, listing the advice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens with the book's own advice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk marks the advice as easy talk, not a plan.

storyboard.claim: No-meeting Wednesdays and pushing back on the boss suit only founders and consultants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz points again with the same knowing smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of advice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the advice to a privileged job type, which the narration then names.

storyboard.claim: The discussion moves from the privileged professional to the real economy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader thinking, a pivot in the frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot after the founder and consultant list.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the shift to workers with no schedule control.

storyboard.claim: A single parent working two hourly jobs just to pay rent has no time to manage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worn worker slumped in a hospital corridor, the shift-worker reader.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the real-economy pivot a face.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hospital set places the hourly shift without a family icon, which would read as abstract shapes.

storyboard.claim: Warehouse workers and junior associates are controlled by algorithms and micromanaging bosses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains binding a worker below, a hand above them pulling the chain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the controlling employer to the single parent.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer reads as one party controlling another, the literal sense of being managed.

storyboard.claim: A boss demands replies late at night, and refusing work can cost you the job.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A modern phone icon with a worker thinking about it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the demand that the 1440 tactic cannot stop.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone reads as a modern smartphone, the always-on message pressure.

storyboard.claim: The entire framework strains and sometimes shatters against low-wage reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz slumped, the defeated face of a system that does not hold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the sentence about the low-value work refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the framework failing in a person, without a breakdown icon the viewer would misread.

storyboard.claim: Without control of your schedule, the billionaire secrets cannot be carried out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried reader thinking over the limit on their schedule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the huge caveat that the previous beats built toward.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the missing condition directly.

storyboard.claim: Even under restricted autonomy, the internal mindset of the framework can protect you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon with a reader thinking about it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pivot: even restricted, something remains.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection, the lifeline sense of the sentence.

storyboard.claim: Pick the one tiny task that moves you toward escape, like updating your resume.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon with a reader pointing at it, hopeful.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the protection idea into one concrete action.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target reads as aiming at a goal, which is what the task is for.

storyboard.claim: Writing worries down on a calendar keeps them from ruining sleep, and breathing reclaims energy on a chaotic shift.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader holding notes, writing down worries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists small adaptable tools inside a rigid job.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes object shows the writing act the callout describes.

storyboard.claim: Protect whatever sliver of agency you have over your mind and time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader holding a key, the small territory they keep.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the tools into a principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key stands for the agency the narration says to defend.

storyboard.claim: The deep dive into the 1440 minutes reaches its payoff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock icon, the time frame of the whole conversation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition into the closing argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock reads as time, matching the 1440-minute framing.

storyboard.claim: Time is a decision problem, not a scheduling problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: decision problem and scheduling problem.
storyboard.onScreenText: The decision problem, not the scheduling problem
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalls the thesis from the start of the conversation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sorter shows the two categories the thesis separates.

storyboard.claim: A calendar is not just a digital list of burdens; time is consumed through choices.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader holding a phone with a calendar, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the thesis to the calendar.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone shows the digital calendar being reframed.

storyboard.claim: A calendar is the most honest mirror, showing where your minutes actually go.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock over a calendar, showing where the minutes actually go.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the calendar into the central metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror reads as self-reflection, the honest self-check the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: A stranger reading your calendar would infer your core values from where your minutes go.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader speaking, the question put to them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Develops the mirror: what a stranger would see.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question carries the claim; no icon would read correctly for relatives or values.

storyboard.claim: A frantic calendar serves other people's emergencies instead of your own priorities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz slumped, the uncomfortable truth of the calendar.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the mirror image with the uncomfortable result.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cost in a face rather than an abstract monument.

storyboard.claim: Your minutes reveal what you truly prioritize, whatever goals you claim.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader pointing at the viewer with a knowing smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the final provocative thought.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk frames the provocation as a pointed question to the viewer.

storyboard.claim: So far the talk covered outside defenses: blocking time, saying no, handling bosses and clients.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader pointing outward at the people who take time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the final thought by contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: The outward point marks the difference between outside and inside.

storyboard.claim: The elephant trampling your time may be internal rather than an external force.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader thinking, weighing the inner cause.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question that opens the internal turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the reversal; an elephant icon would read as nothing.

storyboard.claim: The time thief is your own fear of sitting down to finish your most important task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader with a frightened face, thinking about the task.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the internal cause the question raised.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face shows fear, which surprised would misread as wonder.

storyboard.claim: Sometimes we intentionally choose to be crazy busy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader speaking, the admission of choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the deliberate choice to the fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout makes the choice explicit, since the face is neutral.

storyboard.claim: A 70-item to-do list at high speed gives you a socially acceptable excuse for not achieving dreams.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz on a highway with a road icon, rushing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Illustrates the choice to be busy with the highway from the opening.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road reads as the literal highway, the 80 mph rush of the opening.

storyboard.claim: Being always buried in email gives a reason you never reach your real dreams.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader slumped holding a phone, buried in messages.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the concrete form of the busy excuse.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone shows the email source; the slump shows being overwhelmed.

storyboard.claim: Staying busy means you never have to find out how good your best effort really is.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader with a frightened face, thinking about the untested effort.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Final payoff of the busy-excuse argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout states the consequence; the afraid face carries the stake.
